text:
The San Jose Sharks almost didn't make this one. Their plane to Utah never left on Friday when the FAA grounded every flight in the country over a communications issue; Sharks Hockey Digest reported the team deplaned, and Sheng Peng of San Jose Hockey Now later reported they were cleared to fly Friday night. So the Sharks arrive late, on the first night of a back-to-back, after a 3-2 shootout loss to Pittsburgh in which Macklin Celebrini reached 200 career points and Ivar Stenberg hit three posts.

Celebrini is the reason to watch San Jose at all right now: our numbers have him at 43% to score and 83% for a point, the best on either side. Stenberg, the second pick in June, is on the top power play with him, per San Jose Hockey Now's Sheng Peng. Will Smith is one goal from 50 for his career. The problem is everything behind them. The Sharks allow more expected goals per 60 than anyone, and Yaroslav Askarov (7.0 goals better than expected) has been holding it together.

Utah is in a worse spot than its 57% share of the five-on-five chances suggests. The Mammoth are winless in four, and over that stretch the chances say they earned it: 42% of the expected goals. The injuries explain a lot. Logan Cooley (21 points in 18 games) is out again tonight, per CBS Sports, Dylan Guenther is on injured reserve for two to four weeks, and Nate Schmidt is out. Nick Schmaltz is day to day. Clayton Keller has moved up beside Vincent Trocheck and Lawson Crouse, Kailer Yamamoto is playing 19 minutes a night, up from 13, and Trocheck is one assist from 400. Karel Vejmelka, 4.3 goals worse than expected this season, is projected to start after Thursday's shootout loss in which he stopped all 22 shots.

Our numbers give Utah the better chances, 3.74 expected goals to 2.87, and give the Mammoth a 70% shot at the playoffs. San Jose is at 5%.
headline: Sharks beat the ground stop, Mammoth count injuries
